newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba's Stinnes unit sees lower 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Veba's Stinnes unit sees lower 1996 profit.

text.p: Stinnes AG, the large trading and transport unit of German utility giant Veba AG, said late on Monday it expected profits for the current year to be lower than in 1995.
"Last year's result will not quite be reached," Stinnes chief Helmut Mamsch said at a news briefing.
He added that while 1996 profits would not quite match those of 1995, when it made a pre-tax gain of 252.3 million marks, the pre-tax figure for this year would not be below 200 million marks.
Stinnes, which trades a number of products from steel to oil, said it expected a 1996 turnover of 21.24 billion marks compared to just over 22 billion marks last year.
Veba itself said earlier this month it was expecting a 25 percent rise in net profits from last year's 1.9 billion marks.
